title: Plan and write per-clip .alc files; folder lifecycle; --no-clips
description:
## Intent
Per-clip `.alc` content and the folder's lifecycle.

## Scope
- `apricity-daw::export::plan_clip_files(sample, folder_listing) -> Vec<Outcome>`: one `.alc` per active (not retired) saved clip (region = `start..end`, loop on, markers inside the region plus interpolated end markers, warp mode per §Mapping, detune as the sample); retired clips skipped.
- Lifecycle: files Apricity wrote carry the clip's name as the `.alc` clip name; on re-export, a file whose content equals what Apricity last would write for a clip that no longer exists (deleted or renamed) is removed; a file whose markers or region differ from Apricity's is kept and reported (`--force` replaces).
- `apricity-cli`: `--no-clips`; report lines per clip and the summary.

## Verify
`safe-run.sh -- cargo test -p apricity-daw -p apricity-cli` (all M3 scenarios green).

Commit: `feat(<this id>): export saved clips as .alc files`.

---
**Toolchain:** every Bash call starts with `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`; run builds and tests under the watchdog: `safe-run.sh -- <command>` (6 GB / 20 min cap; do not edit it). At most two Rust-building agents at once.
**Protocol:** specs first (write the scenario, watch it fail, then code); keep a running log with `kbs comment` (decisions, problems, attempts, outcomes); paste the tail of **Verify** before asking for review; never commit, push or close (the reviewer does, after re-running Verify). Never write the DAW's brand name anywhere.
